question.text: Drift speed of electrons, when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1.5</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> current flows in a copper wire of cross section <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mi> </mi><msup><mi>mm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>.</mo></math> If the electron density in copper is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>28</mn></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is close to (Take charge of an electron to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1.6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></msup><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>)

Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : For measuring the potential difference across a resistance of 600 Ω, the voltmeter with resistance 1000 Ω will be preferred over voltmeter with resistance 4000 Ω.

Reason R : Voltmeter with higher resistance will draw smaller current than voltmeter with lower resistance.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below

options.text: A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
